# Equivalence with Appendix A of Laureshyn et al. (2010)

*Generated by `tools/equivalence.py`; do not edit by hand.* pyssms 0.1.0, Python 3.13.5, NumPy 2.5.4, seed 2026, horizon 60 s.

## 1. Generic encounters (random approach angles)

1,000,000 random encounters of cars, pedestrians, cyclists and trucks (states A/B/C: 315,080 / 627,161 / 57,759). 12,305 start with overlapping bodies, which the appendix does not treat, and 0 have parallel paths; 987,695 are compared.

| indicator | encounters that disagree |
|---|---|
| ttc | 0 |
| tadv | 0 |
| t2 | 0 |
| tg | 0 |
| first | 0 |

Tolerance: 1e-6 s absolute or 1e-7 relative. Run time for all four indicators (measured while other work was running; use benchmark.md for speed): time-time polygon 5.83 s, 32 corner-side combinations (vectorised over encounters) 20.69 s.

**Sign of Eqs. (8)-(9).** The author's 2010 thesis (Appendix, printed p. 138) prints these equations with a leading minus sign, which is what substituting Eq. (4) into Eq. (6) gives; the "article in press" PDF of the journal paper omits it, so that form returns minus the crossing time. This is therefore a typesetting difference of the preprint, not an error of the method; the final journal version was not checked. For a reader who codes the appendix from the preprint: with the preprint form the procedure finds a TTC in 8,290 of the compared encounters, of which 0 equal the true TTC; the true number of collision courses is 302,775.

## 2. Axis-aligned bodies and the in-section test of Eq. (10)

* `tol=0`: compared 49,731; disagreements {'ttc': 6730, 'tadv': 3200, 't2': 5723, 'tg': 0, 'first': 3200}
* `tol=1e-09`: compared 49,731; disagreements {'ttc': 0, 'tadv': 0, 't2': 0, 'tg': 0, 'first': 0}

With a side parallel to an axis, Eq. (10) asks for an exact equality of floating-point coordinates; a literal implementation (tol = 0) then misses contacts.

## 3. Cases outside the appendix: grid oracle

Brute force on a (tau1, tau2) grid (horizon 30 s for both methods) with the separating-axis test, independent of the half-plane code. Agreement means equal within two grid steps or both undefined.

| kind | covered by appendix | oracle cases | TTC agree | TAdv agree | TG agree | max diff (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| parallel | 0 / 100,000 | 300 | 300 | 299 | 300 | 0.020 |
| stopped | 0 / 100,000 | 300 | 300 | 300 | 300 | 0.020 |
| overlap | 100,000 / 100,000 | 300 | 300 | 300 | 300 | 0.024 |

One of the 300 parallel cases differs in TAdv (package: undefined, grid: 2.6 s). The paths are almost parallel, so the minimum of |tau1 - tau2| lies along an edge of K that is almost parallel to the diagonal; its true minimiser is at the horizon edge, which the package reports as undefined by rule, while the grid sees quantised ties inside the horizon. Documented, not tuned away.
